## Lesson 3 — Request the named two-Port S21 trace {#lesson-ch3-s21}

### Declare one finite sample grid and one channel

Read [Simulation conventions](../../../docs/concepts/simulation-conventions.qmd#matrix-axes-and-power-waves)
for the output-row/input-column channel direction and wave reference.

The selected network is `run.original`: the complete main Plan has exactly the
two terminated feedline Ports needed by this request. `transmission` names the
output-from-input projection of the complete Direct S matrix; it does not
launch a separate solve.

```{python}
#| id: ch3-prepare-direct-s21
run = CircuitRun(plan=plan, storage="memory")
view = run.original
sample_frequencies = [5.5, 6.0, 6.5] * u.GHz
transmission_trace = SParameterTrace(
    id="transmission",
    input_port="feedline_in",
    input_mode=(),
    output_port="feedline_out",
    output_mode=(),
)
direct_spec = DirectSolveSpec(
    frequencies=sample_frequencies,
    traces=(transmission_trace,),
)
```

Compiler explanations are covered in the advanced [Workspace lesson](../chapter-08/chapter.qmd).

The grid contains exactly three declared samples. Lines drawn between them are
presentation only: this lesson does not infer a continuous resonance, locate a
dip, interpolate, or evaluate an undeclared frequency.

```{python}
#| id: ch3-solve-direct-s21
direct = run.solve(view, direct_spec)
transmission = direct.traces["transmission"]
```

`transmission.value` retains the complex dimensionless S21 values. The plot
below shows magnitude in dB, while the generated CSV preserves real and
imaginary parts at every declared frequency.

```{python}
#| id: ch3-show-direct-s21
display(direct.s.view)
display(transmission.frequencies)
display(transmission.value)
from IPython.display import display

magnitude_plot = transmission.plot(component="magnitude", magnitude="db")
phase_plot = transmission.plot(component="phase")
for figure, component, unit in (
    (magnitude_plot, "magnitude", "dB"),
    (phase_plot, "phase", "deg"),
):
    figure.update_traces(
        mode="lines+markers", line={"color": "#246398", "width": 2},
        marker={"color": "#246398", "size": 7},
        hovertemplate="%{x:.6g} GHz<br>%{y:.6g} " + unit + "<extra></extra>",
    )
    figure.update_layout(
        template="plotly_white", autosize=True, height=340, showlegend=False,
        title={"text": f"S21 {component}", "x": .02, "xanchor": "left", "font": {"size": 18}},
        font={"family": "Arial, sans-serif", "size": 14, "color": "#243344"},
        margin={"l": 78, "r": 24, "t": 55, "b": 62},
        paper_bgcolor="white", plot_bgcolor="white",
    )
    figure.update_xaxes(title_text="Frequency (GHz)", ticks="outside", showline=True,
                        linecolor="#6f7b85", gridcolor="#e5e9ed", zeroline=False,
                        automargin=True, title_standoff=12)
    figure.update_yaxes(title_text=f"{component.capitalize()} ({unit})", ticks="outside",
                        showline=True, linecolor="#6f7b85", gridcolor="#e5e9ed",
                        zeroline=False, automargin=True, title_standoff=12)
display(magnitude_plot)
display(phase_plot)
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

Port 1 is `feedline_in` and Port 2 is `feedline_out`; S21 maps input at Port 1 to output at Port 2. The exact samples are 5.5, 6.0 and 6.5 GHz.
